sentences.text: This is claimants appeal against judgment and award passed in MVC No.36/2017 on the file of II Additional senior Civil Judge & MACT-VII, Vijayapura (for short 'the Tribunal'), claiming enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: II Additional senior Civil Judge & MACT-VII, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties will be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
3. It is case of claimants that on 12.09.2016, the deceased Samadhan Pawar was returning to his village in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.MH-13/BS-6383 and he was riding the said vehicle.
At Brahmapuri bus stand, he met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Reg.No.CG-04/JC-8951 by its driver.
Due to the impact he sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.

It is further case of the claimants that deceased was aged about 38 years at the time of accident; he was an agriculturist and milk vendor; and earning Rs.50,000/- per NC:
2023:KHC-K:4844-DB month.
Claimants were depending his earnings.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.90,50,000/-.
4. Respondent No.2 insurer denied all the contention of claimants and it prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues.
6. The Tribunal has recorded evidence.
Claimants examined PW1 and PW2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
Respondents have not lead evidence.
7. The Tribunal after hearing the arguments and on appreciating the pleadings and evidence, held that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry by its driver.

The Tribunal has also assessed age of deceased as 38 years, his earnings as Rs.7,000/- per month and applied multiplier as 15 and deducted 1/4th of earnings of NC: 2023:KHC-K:4844-DB the deceased towards personal expenses and awarded the compensation as under:
Loss of income due to : Rs.9,45,000/- dependency Loss of spousal, parental and :
Rs.2,00,000/-
 filial consortium  Loss of estate : Rs.15,000/-
 Transportation and funeral : Rs.15,000/-
 expenses  Total : Rs.11,75,000/-
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have preferred this appeal, praying for enhancement of compensation.
8. The matter is posted for hearing on admission and with the consent of both the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal.

sentences.text: We have heard the arguments of learned advocates for both side.

10. The learned advocate for the appellants has contended that the Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month, though the contention of appellants was that deceased was earning NC: 2023:KHC-K:4844-DB Rs.50,000/- per month from agriculture and milk vending.

He has further stated that even if it is held that the claimants were unable to prove their income, atleast Tribunal could have considered the income on the basis of guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority while settlement of the dispute in Lok-Adalat; According to which the income of deceased could be taken at Rs.8,750/-.
He has further submitted that the Tribunal has not considered future prospects of the deceased.
He was aged about 38 years, therefore the Tribunal ought to have added 40% of the income of deceased towards future prospects and awarded the compensation.
He has further submitted that there is no dispute regarding the amount of compensation awarded under other heads.
Hence, prayed to allow the appeal.
11. The learned advocate for respondent-insurer has supported the impugned judgment and submitted that there are no reasons to interfere in the said findings.

The following point emerges for determination:
"Whether the appellants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
13.
The Tribunal by appreciating the pleadings and evidence, held that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry by its driver and it is not disputed.
Undisputedly the age of deceased was 38 years.
Before the Tribunal claimants were unable to prove that deceased was earning Rs.50,000/- per month from his occupation.
As rightly submitted by the learned advocate for the appellants, income of the deceased taken by the Tribunal is on lower side.

While settlement of cases pertaining to motor vehicle compensation before the Lok- Adalat, income of victim of an accident, which taken place during the year 2016, is taken at Rs.8,750/-; Same could be applied to the present case.
14. The Tribunal has not taken future prospects of the deceased.
He was aged about 38 years.
As held in the NC: 2023:KHC-K:4844-DB case of National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others1, below the age of 40 years future prospects has to be considered at the rate of 40%.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V. Pranay Sethi and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, 40% of his income has to be added towards future prospects which amounts to Rs.3,500/-.

There were five dependents to the deceased, therefore as rightly held by the Tribunal,
1/4th of his income has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Multiplier applicable to the case in hand is 15.

From the above said calculations, the claimants are entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is Rs.9,188/- X 12 X 15 = Rs.16,58,840/-.
15.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, which does not call for any interference.

2017 ACJ 2700 NC: 2023:KHC-K:4844-DB 1.

2. Loss of consortium - Rs.2,00,000/-
3. Loss of estate - Rs.15,000/-
4.

Total - Rs.18,83,840/-

The claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.7,08,840/-
.
17.

For aforesaid reasons, we answer the point in issue in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is partly allowed, with costs.
ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.36/2017 dated 22.09.2021 is modified.

(a) Claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,83,840/- as against Rs.11,75,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal and claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.07,08,840/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of petition till its payment.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:4844-DB (b) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the said amount of compensation within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this award.
(c) The orders passed by the Tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release of the amount is not disturbed.
